[11] Lifetime Revenue Loss Projection
Description: Estimates the total potential revenue loss over a plant's expected lifetime due to its ongoing annual degradation.
Definition: A projection of future losses based on the Annual Degradation Rate (ADR). A simplified model is: $LRL = \text{ADR} \times \text{Annual Energy Production} \times \text{Energy Price} \times \text{Remaining Lifetime}$.

Description: Calculates the efficiency loss of a solar panel due to its operating temperature exceeding the reference temperature.
Definition: The reduction in efficiency caused by cell temperature, calculated as: $L_{T} = (T_{cell} - T_{ref}) \times |\gamma|$, where $T_{cell}$ is the current cell temperature, $T_{ref}$ is the reference temperature (typically 25°C), and $\gamma$ is the panel's temperature coefficient of power.

[10] Temperature-Corrected Performance
Description: Estimates the performance of a solar asset if thermal losses were eliminated.
Definition: The asset's power output adjusted for temperature effects, providing a clearer view of performance irrespective of thermal conditions. Calculated as: $P_{corrected} = \frac{P_{actual}}{1 - \text{Thermal Loss Factor}}$.

rc_round1.derivation: Compute the snapshot's thermal loss factor from its operating cell temperature, the 25°C reference temperature, and the absolute temperature coefficient of power, then compute temperature-corrected performance as actual power output divided by one minus that thermal loss factor.

Definition: An index representing the cost per unit of capacity, calculated as: $OEI = \frac{C_{maint} + C_{clean} + C_{replace}}{P_{rated}}$, where C represents costs and $P_{rated}$ is the plant's rated power.

Definition: The ratio of power lost to the total power generated, calculated as: $R_{loss} = \frac{P_{loss}}{P_{output} + P_{loss}}$.

question: Let's get a financial forecast for our worst panels, the ones that degrade so fast they'll lose over 14% of their power in 20 years. [7] Annual Degradation Rate (ADR)
Description: Calculates the average yearly percentage loss in a solar plant's performance or efficiency since its commissioning.
Definition: The annualized rate of performance loss, calculated as: $ADR = \frac{\text{Cumulative Degradation Pct}}{\text{Age in Years}}$.

[11] Lifetime Revenue Loss Projection
Description: Estimates the total potential revenue loss over a plant's expected lifetime due to its ongoing annual degradation.
Definition: A projection of future losses based on the Annual Degradation Rate (ADR). A simplified model is: $LRL = \text{ADR} \times \text{Annual Energy Production} \times \text{Energy Price} \times \text{Remaining Lifetime}$.

[20] High Degradation Panel Model
Description: Identifies a solar panel model that degrades at a faster rate than the industry average.
Definition: A panel model is considered to have high degradation if its officially specified annual power degradation rate exceeds a certain threshold, for example, 0.7%.

rc_round1.population: Solar panel entities whose annual power degradation rate implies more than 14% cumulative power loss over 20 years, equivalent to a rate greater than 0.7% per year.
rc_round1.row_grain: One global summary representing all qualifying solar panel entities.
rc_round1.column_role: A single monetary total of projected revenue loss.
rc_round1.derivation: For each qualifying panel, compute the 15-year revenue loss as annual degradation fraction × 400,000 MWh × $50 per MWh × 15 years, then sum those losses across all qualifying panels.
rc_round1.filter_policy: none

rc_round2.population: Solar panel model entities whose officially specified annual power degradation rate is greater than 0.7% per year, implying more than 14% cumulative power loss over 20 years.
rc_round2.row_grain: One global summary representing all qualifying solar panel model entities.
rc_round2.column_role: A single monetary total of projected revenue loss.
rc_round2.derivation: For each qualifying panel model, convert its annual power degradation rate from percentage points to a fraction, multiply by 400,000 MWh, $50 per MWh, and 15 years, then sum the resulting projected losses across all qualifying panel models.
rc_round2.filter_policy: none
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata identifies panel_models.degyrrate as the officially specified annual power degradation rate, so the qualifying panels are panel-model entities and the rate is a percentage value. This refines the population and derivation while preserving the global projected-loss total.

question: For the machines that are down more than one day in a 20-day period, what's the average price tag on a single repair? To calculate the mean repair cost, you'll need to figure out how long each machine has been running. Only use data where the mtbf and service time are positive.
evidence:
[4] System Unavailability
Description: Calculates the proportion of time a system is non-operational or in a state of failure.
Definition: The probability that a system will not be operational when needed, calculated using mean time to repair (MTTR) and mean time between failures (MTBF): $U = \frac{MTTR}{MTBF + MTTR}$.

[8] System Availability
Description: Calculates the proportion of time a system is operational and available to perform its required function.
Definition: The probability that a system is operational, calculated as: $A = 1 - \text{System Unavailability}$. A value of 99% implies the system is non-operational for 1% of the time.

[19] Mean Repair Cost
Description: Calculates the average cost associated with a single repair event.
Definition: The total maintenance cost divided by the number of failure events (which can be inferred from the total operational time and MTBF). $C_{repair} = \frac{\text{Total Maintenance Cost}}{\text{Total Time} / MTBF}$.

[33] Chronic Downtime Asset
Description: An asset that suffers from frequent failures and low operational uptime.
Definition: An asset is classified as having chronic downtime if its System Availability is below a critical threshold, for example, 95%.

rc_round1.population: Contributing machines and their maintenance/repair data are eligible only when MTBF and service time are positive and the machine's estimated downtime, derived from MTBF and service time, exceeds one day in a 20-day period, equivalent to system availability below 95%.
rc_round1.row_grain: One overall summary for the eligible machines.
rc_round1.column_role: A single numeric mean repair cost, representing the average price tag of one repair.
rc_round1.derivation: Estimate each eligible machine's operational running time within the 20-day period, infer repair counts from running time divided by MTBF, and compute the eligible population's mean repair cost as total maintenance cost divided by the total inferred repair counts.
rc_round1.filter_policy: none

rc_round2.population: Contributing machines and their maintenance/repair data are eligible only when MTBF and service time (mean time to repair) are positive hourly values, and the machine's estimated downtime over a 20-day (480-hour) period, derived from MTBF and MTTR, exceeds one day (24 hours), equivalent to system availability below 95%.
rc_round2.row_grain: One overall summary for the eligible machines.
rc_round2.column_role: A single numeric mean repair cost, representing the average price tag of one repair.
rc_round2.derivation: Using hourly MTBF and MTTR, estimate availability as MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR), estimate each eligible machine's running time over the 480-hour period as availability multiplied by 480, infer repair counts from running time divided by MTBF, and compute the eligible population's mean repair cost as total maintenance cost divided by the total inferred repair counts.
rc_round2.filter_policy: none
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata confirms that MTBF and mean time to repair are recorded as hourly operational metrics, so service time is MTTR and the 20-day window is 480 hours. This resolves the unit basis for downtime eligibility and running-time estimation.

question: After accounting for all the power being lost inside the system, what was the actual usable power output for snapshot 'pv945724'? Give me the final number in watts.

Description: Measures the proportion of power that is generated but lost within the system before reaching the grid.

Description: Calculates the net power delivered by the system after accounting for internal power losses.
Definition: The actual usable power from a system, derived from its gross output and its System Power Loss Ratio. It is calculated as: $P_{eff} = P_{gross} \times (1 - \text{System Power Loss Ratio})$.

[1] Transaction Velocity Rate
Description: Measures transaction completion speed.

Description: Efficiency of data protection per vulnerability.

Description: Represents vendor's compliance performance.
Definition: CEI = \frac{\text{compliance\_score}}{\text{violation\_count}}

[4] Anonymity Cost Index
Description: Traceability score per anonymity level.
Definition: ACI = \frac{\text{traceability\_cost}}{\text{anonymity\_score}}

Description: Risk per dollar spent by a buyer.

Definition: Any transaction where the shipment passes from one country to another, triggering customs or import controls.

Description: Liquidity as a function of transaction flow and price.
Definition: PLR = \frac{\text{successful\_txns} \times \text{average\_price}}{\text{days\_active}}

Description: How efficiently threats are managed over time.
Definition: THR = \frac{\text{threats\_handled}}{\text{total\_hours}}

Description: Defines the environmental conditions considered optimal for archaeological scanning based on instrument sensitivity profiles.
Definition: Conditions with \text{ESI} > 85, where ESI is the Environmental Suitability Index (knowledge #7), characterized by moderate temperature, humidity around 50%, and good illumination, minimizing environmental interference with scanning accuracy.

[50] Environmental Condition Classification System (ECCS)
Description: A comprehensive classification system for archaeological site environments based on their suitability for scanning operations.
Definition: A four-tier classification where 'Optimal Scanning Conditions' have \text{ESI} > 85, 'Good Scanning Conditions' have ESI between 70-85, 'Acceptable Scanning Conditions' have ESI between 50-70, and 'Challenging Scanning Conditions' have ESI < 50. Description: A binary classification system that determines if equipment has met all necessary conditions to safely operate during extreme weather events.

Let's just focus on the 'Safety' type equipment and sort it by the best reliability score.

[1] Operational Readiness Score (ORS)
Description: Quantifies how ready equipment is for immediate deployment based on operational status and maintenance schedule.
Definition: ORS = \begin{cases} 10 \times (1 - \frac{\text{operation hours}}{\text{maintenance cycle hours}}) & \text{if operational status = 'Active'} \\ 5 \times (1 - \frac{\text{operation hours}}{\text{maintenance cycle hours}}) & \text{if operational status = 'Standby'} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

[6] Thermal Insulation Efficiency (TIE)
Description: Measures how effectively a structure retains heat based on insulation status and heat loss rate.
Definition: TIE = \begin{cases} 0.9 - \frac{\text{heat loss rate (kWh)}}{10} & \text{if insulation status = 'Good'} \\ 0.6 - \frac{\text{heat loss rate (kWh)}}{10} & \text{if insulation status = 'Fair'} \\ 0.3 - \frac{\text{heat loss rate (kWh)}}{10} & \text{if insulation status = 'Poor'} \end{cases}, \text{ where lower heat loss and better insulation result in higher efficiency.}

[33] Life Support System Reliability (LSSR)
Description: Evaluates the reliability of life support systems under polar conditions
Definition: LSSR = 0.7 \times ORS + 0.3 \times TIE

[51] Life Support Reliability Classification (LSRC)
Description: Categorizes life support systems into reliability classes based on their LSSR score for operational decision-making.
Definition: Life support systems are classified into three reliability categories: 'High Reliability' WHEN (LSSR >= 0.8), 'Moderate Reliability' WHEN (LSSR >= 0.6 AND LSSR < 0.8), and 'Low Reliability' WHEN (LSSR < 0.6).

[9] Renewable Energy Contribution (REC)
Description: Calculates the percentage contribution of renewable energy sources to the total power generation.
Definition: REC = \frac{\text{solar output (W)} + \text{wind output (W)}}{\text{fuel cell output (W)} + \text{solar output (W)} + \text{wind output (W)}} \times 100, \text{ where higher values indicate greater reliance on renewable energy.}

Description: Defines the conditions for energy-sustainable operations in polar environments.
Definition: An operation is considered 'Energy-Sustainable' when it maintains a REC above 70% (meaning more than 70% of energy comes from renewable sources) while maintaining full operational capability and adequate power reserves for at least 48 hours in case of emergency.

Description: A comprehensive classification system that categorizes operational energy sustainability based on renewable energy contribution percentages.

question: Let's get a handle on our water situation at each station. For each station, can you tell me its name and location type? I need to see the average water quality score, the average water management score, and a count of how many systems are in 'conservation needed' mode. Also, give me a simple classification for both the water quality and the overall management status. Sort the list with the best-managed stations at the top.
evidence:
[7] Water Resource Management Index (WRMI)
Description: Evaluates the efficiency of water resource management based on water levels, quality, and waste levels.
Definition: WRMI = \frac{\text{water level percent}}{100} \times \frac{\text{water quality index}}{100} \times (1 - \frac{\text{waste tank level percent}}{100}), \text{ where higher water quality and appropriate water/waste levels indicate better management.}

[18] Water Conservation Requirement
Description: Specifies the conditions under which water conservation measures must be implemented.
Definition: Water conservation measures must be implemented when the WRMI falls below 0.5, indicating either low water levels, poor water quality, or high waste tank levels that require immediate attention to maintain sustainable water usage.

[25] Water Quality Classification System (WQCS)
Description: A standardized system that categorizes water quality for health, safety, and operational purposes in polar environments.
Definition: Water is classified into five quality categories based on its quality index: 'High-Quality' WHEN (water quality index >= 91), suitable for all purposes including direct consumption; 'Good' WHEN (water quality index >= 71 AND water quality index < 91), safe for consumption after standard treatment; 'Moderate' WHEN (water quality index >= 51 AND water quality index < 71), acceptable for washing but not consumption; 'Poor' WHEN (water quality index >= 26 AND water quality index < 51), suitable only for limited non-contact uses; 'Unsafe' WHEN (water quality index < 26), unsuitable for any use and requiring immediate remediation.

[53] Water Resource Management Status Classification (WRMSC)
Description: A comprehensive classification system that categorizes water resource management status based on WRMI values to guide operational decisions.
Definition: Water management operations are classified into three status levels: 'Conservation Needed' WHEN (WRMI < 0.5), indicating critical resource limitations requiring immediate conservation measures; 'Monitoring Advised' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.5 AND WRMI < 0.7), representing adequate but vigilant management requiring regular system monitoring; 'Sustainable Management' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.7), indicating optimal water resource utilization suitable for unrestricted operations.

rc_round1.population: Target population is all stations; station metrics draw on water quality scores and WRMI values associated with each station, and the conservation count considers station-associated systems whose WRMI is below 0.5.

rc_round1.derivation: For each station, average its associated water quality scores and its associated WRMI values, count its systems with WRMI below 0.5, classify the average water quality score using the WQCS thresholds, classify the average WRMI using the WRMSC thresholds, and treat WRMI as water level percent / 100 * water quality index / 100 * (1 - waste tank level percent / 100).
rc_round1.filter_policy: Order stations by average water management score descending because higher WRMI indicates better management; no limit or tie-breaking is specified.

rc_round2.derivation: For each station, average the water quality index values and WRMI values from its associated water-and-waste data, count its systems with WRMI below 0.5, classify the average water quality score using the WQCS thresholds, classify the average WRMI using the WRMSC thresholds, and compute WRMI as water level percent / 100 * water quality index / 100 * (1 - waste tank level percent / 100).

[4] Communication Reliability Index (CRI)
Description: Assesses the reliability of communication systems based on signal metrics and antenna status.
Definition: CRI = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if antenna status = 'Error'} \\ 5 & \text{if antenna status = 'Warning'} \\ 10 & \text{if antenna status = 'Normal'} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \times (1 - \frac{\text{signal latency (ms)}}{1000}), \text{ where lower latency and better antenna status result in higher reliability.}

[11] Event Participation Score (EPS)
Description: A weighted score that measures a fan's engagement with platform events, prioritizing in-person attendance.
Definition: EPS = (\text{Online Events} \times 1) + (\text{Offline Events} \times 1.5) + (\text{Meet-and-Greets} \times 2)

[30] Event Enthusiast
Description: A fan who actively and frequently participates in a wide range of platform events, especially high-value ones like meet-and-greets.

Description: An elite fan who combines high spending with high event participation, representing the most dedicated segment of the user base.
Definition: A fan is an Idol Superfan if they are classified as both a Whale Fan and an Event Enthusiast.

[59] Cumulative Spending
Description: The running total of a fan's spending up to a specific point in time.
Definition: A value calculated using a window function (SUM OVER PARTITION BY fan ORDER BY date) on time-ordered interaction data, specifically summing the Total Gift Value in USD from interaction gifts.

[60] Spending Velocity Cohort Analysis
Description: An analysis that measures the average Cumulative Spending for a defined group of fans at specific time milestones after their registration.

question:
Let's dig into the files of patients who are getting positive crossmatch results.
I need a list of these folks.
For each one, show me their ID, their PRA score, and whether they have those donor-specific antibodies.
Then, based on our official rules for Antibody-Mediated Rejection (AMR) Risk Stratification, tell me if they're considered 'High Risk'.
Oh, and I also want to see the date of the last time we tried to find a match for them.
Sort the whole thing so the most sensitized patients are at the top.
evidence:
[22] Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) Typing
Description: The process of identifying specific HLA protein markers on a person's cells to match a donor with a recipient for transplantation.
Definition: A genetic test that identifies a person's unique HLA markers. A closer HLA match between a donor and recipient reduces the risk of the recipient's immune system attacking, or rejecting, the transplanted organ.

[24] Crossmatch Test
Description: A final compatibility test performed just before transplant surgery to ensure the recipient has no pre-formed antibodies against the specific donor's tissues.
Definition: A laboratory test that directly mixes the recipient's serum with the donor's lymphocytes. A 'positive' Crossmatch Test indicates the presence of donor-specific antibodies and is a contraindication to transplantation, as it predicts immediate organ rejection.

[26] Donor-Specific Antibodies (DSA)
Description: Antibodies in a recipient's blood that are specifically directed against a particular donor's HLA antigens.
Definition: The presence of these antibodies is identified by a positive Crossmatch Test. They pose a significant risk for antibody-mediated rejection of the transplanted organ.

[23] Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA)
Description: A test that measures the level of pre-existing antibodies in a recipient's blood against common HLA antigens, indicating their sensitization level.
Definition: A measure of a recipient's sensitization to foreign HLA antigens, represented by the `pra_score`[cite: 36]. For matching purposes, a recipient with a `pra_score` of 80 or higher is defined as having a 'high PRA score', indicating a state of high immunological sensitization.

[51] Antibody-Mediated Rejection (AMR) Risk Stratification
Description: A system for categorizing a recipient's risk of developing antibody-mediated rejection based on their immunological profile.
Definition: A risk classification system. For recipients who have a 'Positive' crossmatch result, the 'High Risk' category is defined by meeting two concurrent criteria: having a Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) score of 80 or greater AND having a 'Positive' donor-specific antibody (DSA) status. Recipients not meeting these criteria are considered 'Standard Risk'.

[29] Immunological Sensitization
Description: A state where a recipient has a high level of pre-formed antibodies, making it difficult to find a compatible donor.
Definition: A clinical state where a recipient is considered highly sensitized to potential donors. This condition is formally defined as having a Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) score of 80 or greater. This high level of sensitization significantly complicates the matching process by severely limiting the number of compatible donors.

rc_round1.population: Eligible patients are recipients who have at least one positive crossmatch test result.
rc_round1.row_grain: One row represents one eligible patient.
rc_round1.column_role: The result must show the patient identifier, the patient's PRA score, the patient's donor-specific antibody status, an indicator of whether the patient is High Risk under AMR risk stratification, and the date of the patient's most recent donor-matching attempt.
rc_round1.derivation: For each patient, donor-specific antibody presence is interpreted according to the supplied positive-crossmatch definition, AMR risk is High Risk when the PRA score is at least 80 and donor-specific antibody status is positive and otherwise Standard Risk, and the matching-attempt date is the latest date among that patient's matching attempts.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Order rows by descending PRA score so that more sensitized patients appear first, with tie-breaking unspecified.

rc_round2.population: Eligible patients are recipients whose recorded crossmatch result is Positive.
rc_round2.row_grain: One row represents one eligible patient.
rc_round2.column_role: The result must show the patient identifier, the patient's PRA score, the patient's donor-specific antibody status, an indicator of whether the patient is High Risk under AMR risk stratification, and the date of the patient's most recent donor-matching attempt.
rc_round2.derivation: For each patient, use the patient's recorded PRA score and donor-specific antibody status. AMR risk is High Risk when the PRA score is at least 80 and the donor-specific antibody status is Positive; otherwise it is Standard Risk. The matching-attempt date is the latest date among that patient's matching attempts.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Order rows by descending PRA score so that more sensitized patients appear first, with tie-breaking unspecified.
rc_round2.meta_review: Recipients_Immunology establishes recipient-level cross_result and dsa_state, resolving that positive-crossmatch eligibility and donor-specific antibody status are recorded patient-level attributes. This supports deriving AMR risk from the recorded PRA score and DSA status.

question: I need the pancreas waiting list, sorted exactly how the official Allocation Policy says we should for all the pending matches. Show me the patient's ID, what region they're in, their exact urgency status, the HLA mismatch number, and their final rank in their local area.
evidence:
[25] Medical Urgency Status
Description: A classification system used to prioritize patients on the transplant waiting list based on their immediate need and risk of mortality.
Definition: A tiered system that reflects how critically ill a patient is. For calculation purposes, statuses are mapped to numerical values: Status 1A is assigned a value of 5, Status 1B is 4, Status 2 is 3, and Status 3 is 2. All other statuses are assigned a value of 1.

[4] HLA Mismatch Score
Description: Quantifies the degree of immunological difference between a donor and recipient based on Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA).
Definition: A count of the mismatched HLA antigens (A, B, DR) between the donor and recipient. Formula: $S_{mismatch} = \sum_{i \in \{A, B, DR\}} (HLA_i^{donor} \neq HLA_i^{recipient})$

[34] Allocation Policy
Description: The specific versioned set of rules governing organ distribution, used to prioritize recipients.
Definition: The precise set of rules used for organ distribution, identified by a unique version string in the `allc_pol_vers` field, such as 'v2.7'[cite: 73]. Each policy embodies a strict hierarchy of rules. As a formal example, a given policy stipulates that Medical Urgency Status is the primary sorting criterion; for recipients with an identical urgency status, the one with a lower HLA Mismatch Score receives higher priority.

rc_round1.population: All pending pancreas transplant matches on the waiting list that are subject to the official Allocation Policy.
rc_round1.row_grain: One pending pancreas transplant match for a waiting-list patient.
rc_round1.column_role: Patient ID, the patient's region, the exact medical urgency status, the HLA mismatch count, and the final rank within the local area.
rc_round1.derivation: The HLA mismatch count is the number of mismatched HLA A, B, and DR antigens, and the final local-area rank is the match's relative position within its applicable local area under the official Allocation Policy ordering, which prioritizes higher mapped medical urgency values (Status 1A=5, Status 1B=4, Status 2=3, Status 3=2, other=1) and then lower HLA mismatch counts; the official policy version, local-area boundary, and tie or rank-numbering conventions are otherwise unspecified.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Return all eligible pending matches ordered by the official Allocation Policy sorting rules, with no top-k limit or additional relative selection.

rc_round2.population: All pending pancreas transplant matches on the waiting list that are subject to the official Allocation Policy.
rc_round2.row_grain: One pending pancreas transplant match for a waiting-list patient.
rc_round2.column_role: Patient ID, the patient's allocation region, the exact medical urgency status, the HLA mismatch count, and the stored allocation sequence rank within the applicable allocation region.
rc_round2.derivation: The HLA mismatch count is the number of mismatched HLA A, B, and DR antigens, and the local-area rank is the stored sequence number in allocation ranking for the match's allocation region; the official Allocation Policy ordering prioritizes higher mapped medical urgency values (Status 1A=5, Status 1B=4, Status 2=3, Status 3=2, other=1) and then lower HLA mismatch counts, while the official policy version and tie or rank-numbering conventions remain unspecified.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Return all eligible pending matches ordered by the official Allocation Policy sorting rules, with no top-k limit or additional relative selection.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata establishes allocation_details.allc_seq_num as the stored sequence number in allocation ranking and allocation_details.allc_region as the allocation region, resolving the local-area rank representation. It also confirms transplant_matching.org_spec='Pancreas' and match_status='Pending' as the pancreas pending eligibility conditions.

question:
I want to find the lung transplants that were either insanely expensive for the benefit, or a massive bargain.
Could you calculate the Cost-Effectiveness Ratio for all the lung transplants we've finished? For the QALY part of the formula, just use the patient's quality-of-life score and multiply it by 5 years.
Then, rank all of them and split the list into 20 groups. I want to see all the details—match, donor, and recipient IDs, and the final cost-effectiveness number rounded to two decimals—for only the absolute worst group and the absolute best group.
evidence:
[11] Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
Description: A measure of disease burden, including both the quality and the quantity of life lived.
Definition: Calculated by multiplying the years of life by a quality-of-life score. Formula: $QALY = Years_{life} \times Quality_{score}$

[12] Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (CER)
Description: Calculates the cost per unit of health outcome, often using Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY).
Definition: The ratio of the net cost of an intervention to its net health gain. Formula: $CER = \frac{Cost_{net}}{QALY_{gained}}$

[48] Cost-Effectiveness Thresholds
Description: Illustrates typical thresholds for considering a medical intervention as cost-effective.
Definition: A common benchmark for the Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (CER) in the US is $50,000 to $150,000 per Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) gained. Interventions below this threshold are generally considered a good value.

rc_round1.population: Lung transplant cases that are finished.
rc_round1.row_grain: One finished lung transplant case.
rc_round1.column_role: Match identifier, donor identifier, recipient identifier, and the case's final cost-effectiveness ratio expressed to two decimal places.
rc_round1.derivation: For each eligible case, set the QALY to the patient's quality-of-life score multiplied by 5 years, compute the cost-effectiveness ratio as net cost divided by that QALY, and form 20 ranked groups by that ratio.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Return only the group with the lowest cost-effectiveness ratio and the group with the highest cost-effectiveness ratio; the exact 20-way partitioning, group sizes, tie handling, and final order are unspecified.

rc_round2.population: Lung transplant cases that are finished, meaning organ type is Lung and current status is Completed.
rc_round2.row_grain: One finished lung transplant case.
rc_round2.column_role: Match identifier, donor identifier, recipient identifier, and the case's final cost-effectiveness ratio expressed to two decimal places.
rc_round2.derivation: For each eligible case, set the QALY to the patient's recorded quality-of-life assessment score multiplied by 5 years, use the numeric amount of its recorded estimated transplant cost as the net cost, compute the cost-effectiveness ratio as net cost divided by that QALY, and form 20 ranked groups by that ratio.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Return only the group with the lowest cost-effectiveness ratio and the group with the highest cost-effectiveness ratio; the exact 20-way partitioning, group sizes, tie handling, and final order are unspecified.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata resolves finished lung cases via transplant_matching.org_spec = 'Lung' and match_status = 'Completed', and provides case-level risk_evaluation.qol_val and compatibility_metrics.cost_est as the quality-of-life and cost inputs. This refines the eligible population and the metric inputs used to calculate the requested ratio.

question:
Let's see how often we find a perfect match within and between different ethnic groups.
First, you need to identify every single Optimal Donor-Recipient Match we have.
Once you have that list of perfect pairs, I want a table that shows the donor's ethnicity down the side and the recipient's ethnicity across the top, with the cells showing the count of how many times each combination happened.
evidence:
[20] ABO Blood Type Compatibility
Description: Defines the rules for matching blood types between an organ donor and recipient to prevent hyperacute rejection.
Definition: A fundamental matching rule where recipient blood type determines acceptable donor types. Type O is the universal donor; Type AB is the universal recipient. Type A can receive from A and O. Type B can receive from B and O.

[4] HLA Mismatch Score
Description: Quantifies the degree of immunological difference between a donor and recipient based on Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA).
Definition: A count of the mismatched HLA antigens (A, B, DR) between the donor and recipient. Formula: $S_{mismatch} = \sum_{i \in \{A, B, DR\}} (HLA_i^{donor} \neq HLA_i^{recipient})$

[0] Body Mass Index (BMI)
Description: Calculates a person's body mass index from their weight and height.
Definition: BMI is calculated as weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters. Formula: $BMI = \frac{weight_{kg}}{height_m^2}$

[6] Size Compatibility Score
Description: A score that assesses the physical size match between a donor and recipient, primarily using Body Mass Index (BMI).
Definition: A score derived from the ratio of donor and recipient BMI. Formula: $S_{size} = 1 - |\frac{BMI_{donor}}{BMI_{recipient}} - 1|$.

[31] Optimal Donor-Recipient Match
Description: An ideal pairing of a donor and recipient that meets a strict set of criteria to maximize the probability of long-term transplant success.
Definition: An ideal match defined by meeting three specific, stringent criteria simultaneously: 1) Full ABO Blood Type Compatibility. 2) An HLA Mismatch Score of exactly 0. 3) A Size Compatibility Score within the inclusive range of [0.9, 1.1]. A pairing that satisfies all three conditions is classified as an Optimal Donor-Recipient Match.

rc_round1.population: Donor-recipient pairings represented in the data that qualify as Optimal Donor-Recipient Matches: the donor's ABO blood type is compatible with the recipient's blood type under the stated ABO rules, the HLA mismatch score across A, B, and DR is exactly 0, and the BMI-derived size compatibility score is between 0.9 and 1.1 inclusive.
rc_round1.row_grain: One combination of donor ethnicity and recipient ethnicity for which a match count is reported.
rc_round1.column_role: Donor ethnicity as the row category, recipient ethnicity as the column category, and the count of qualifying optimal donor-recipient matches for that ethnicity combination.
rc_round1.derivation: Count the qualifying optimal donor-recipient pairings for each donor-ethnicity and recipient-ethnicity combination to form a cross-tabulated frequency table.
rc_round1.filter_policy: none

rc_round2.population: Donor-recipient pairings represented in the data that qualify as Optimal Donor-Recipient Matches: the donor's ABO blood type is compatible with the recipient's blood type under the stated ABO rules, the HLA mismatch score across A, B, and DR is exactly 0, and the BMI-derived size compatibility score is between 0.9 and 1.1 inclusive.
rc_round2.row_grain: One combination of donor ethnicity and recipient ethnicity for which a match count is reported.

question:
Let's check our CMV exposure risk. I want a list of all current and completed transplants where a CMV-positive donor gave an organ to a CMV-negative patient.
For each of these risky cases, show me the match ID and the transplant center. I also want to see the patient's Infection Risk score from their chart and, right next to it, the average infection risk—rounded to four decimals—for all the non-mismatched transplants done at that same hospital. I want to see if the scores reflect the risk. Please order the results by the hospital's ID.
evidence:
[39] Viral Infection Status
Description: Screening of donors and recipients for key viral infections that can be transmitted or reactivated during transplantation.
Definition: Testing for viruses such as Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV), and Hepatitis. The Viral Infection Status of both donor and recipient is critical for assessing infection risk and planning post-transplant prophylactic treatment.

[25] Medical Urgency Status
Description: A classification system used to prioritize patients on the transplant waiting list based on their immediate need and risk of mortality.
Definition: A tiered system that reflects how critically ill a patient is. For calculation purposes, statuses are mapped to numerical values: Status 1A is assigned a value of 5, Status 1B is 4, Status 2 is 3, and Status 3 is 2. All other statuses are assigned a value of 1.

[45] Medical Urgency Tiers
Description: Illustrates the hierarchy of transplant urgency statuses.
Definition: Patients are prioritized based on their risk of dying while on the waitlist. Status 1A is the highest urgency, reserved for critically ill patients in the ICU. Status 1B is a lower, but still urgent, category. Lower statuses (e.g., Status 2) are for more stable patients.

rc_round1.population: Target population: current or completed transplants where the donor is CMV-positive and the patient is CMV-negative. Reference population: transplants performed at the same hospital as the target transplant that are not CMV-positive donor to CMV-negative patient cases; the question does not impose a current/completed status condition on this reference set.
rc_round1.row_grain: One row per risky target transplant or match.
rc_round1.column_role: The requested output values are the match ID, the transplant center, the target patient's chart infection risk score, and the corresponding hospital-level average infection risk for non-mismatched transplants.
rc_round1.derivation: For each target transplant, use the patient's recorded infection risk score and compute the arithmetic mean of infection risk scores over all reference transplants at the same hospital, rounded to four decimal places.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Return the rows ordered by the hospital ID associated with the transplant center; ordering within the same hospital is unspecified and no limit is requested.

rc_round2.population: Target population: current or completed transplants where the donor's CMV infection status is Positive and the recipient's CMV infection status is Negative. Reference population: transplants performed at the same transplant center as the target transplant that are not CMV-positive donor to CMV-negative recipient cases; the question does not impose a current/completed status condition on this reference set.
rc_round2.row_grain: One row per risky target transplant matching record.
rc_round2.column_role: The requested output values are the match identifier, the transplant center identifier, the target patient's infection risk score for that transplant match, and the corresponding transplant-center-level average infection risk for non-mismatched transplant matching records.
rc_round2.derivation: For each target transplant matching record, use the infection risk assessment score recorded for that match and compute the arithmetic mean of infection risk assessment scores over all reference non-mismatched transplant matching records at the same transplant center, rounded to four decimal places.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Return the rows ordered by the transplant center identification code associated with the target transplant center; ordering within the same center is unspecified and no limit is requested.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata resolves CMV ownership: donor status is medical_history.viralstatinfo.Cmv_State and recipient status is recipients_immunology.cmv_state, while infection risk is the match-level risk_evaluation.riskmetrics.Infect_Risk. It also identifies administrative_and_review.tx_cen_code as the transplant-center identifier used for ordering.

question:
I need a list of our absolute sickest patients—the ones on ECMO or a VAD.
For each of these patients, show me their ID and what kind of life support they're on.
Then, calculate their full Patient Urgency Score. The crucial part is, I want to see their score next to the average score for all the other, more stable patients who are waiting for the same organ, with both scores rounded to four decimals. Let's see how big the gap is. Group the list by organ, and show the sickest patients first within each group.
evidence:
[5] Recipient Wait Time Ratio
Description: Calculates the ratio of a recipient's waiting time to the average waiting time for their specific organ and blood type.
Definition: The recipient's wait time in days converted to years. Formula: $R_{wait} = \frac{T_{recipient_wait_days}}{365.0}$

[25] Medical Urgency Status
Description: A classification system used to prioritize patients on the transplant waiting list based on their immediate need and risk of mortality.
Definition: A tiered system that reflects how critically ill a patient is. For calculation purposes, statuses are mapped to numerical values: Status 1A is assigned a value of 5, Status 1B is 4, Status 2 is 3, and Status 3 is 2. All other statuses are assigned a value of 1.

[14] Patient Urgency Score
Description: A score that quantifies the urgency of a recipient's need for a transplant.
Definition: A composite score based on the recipient's medical urgency status and their Recipient Wait Time Ratio. Formula: $S_{urgency} = 0.7 \times Status_{medical} + 0.3 \times R_{wait}$

rc_round1.population: The target population is patients waiting for an organ who are currently receiving ECMO or a VAD. For each target patient, the reference population is the other more stable patients waiting for the same organ, interpreted as patients waiting for that organ who are not receiving ECMO or a VAD.
rc_round1.row_grain: One target patient, with the same-organ reference average associated with that patient's organ context.
rc_round1.column_role: The result must show the patient identifier, the patient's life-support type or types, the organ grouping, the patient's rounded Patient Urgency Score, and the rounded average Patient Urgency Score for the corresponding reference population.
rc_round1.derivation: Patient Urgency Score is 0.7 times the mapped Medical Urgency Status value (Status 1A = 5, Status 1B = 4, Status 2 = 3, Status 3 = 2, all other statuses = 1) plus 0.3 times recipient wait time in days divided by 365.0; the reference value is the mean of this score over the organ-specific reference population, and both displayed scores are rounded to four decimals.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Rows are grouped by organ and ordered within each organ by higher Patient Urgency Score first; no limit is requested.

rc_round2.population: The target population is patients waiting for an organ who are currently receiving ECMO or a VAD. For each target patient, the reference population is the other more stable patients waiting for the same organ, interpreted as patients waiting for that organ who are not receiving ECMO or a VAD.
rc_round2.row_grain: One target patient, with the same-organ reference average associated with that patient's organ context.
rc_round2.column_role: The result must show the patient identifier, the patient's life-support type or types, the organ grouping, the patient's rounded Patient Urgency Score, and the rounded average Patient Urgency Score for the corresponding reference population.
rc_round2.derivation: Patient Urgency Score is 0.7 times the mapped Medical Urgency Status value (Status 1A = 5, Status 1B = 4, Status 2 = 3, Status 3 = 2, all other statuses = 1), with documented abbreviated forms such as '2' and '3' mapped as Status 2 and Status 3, plus 0.3 times the recipient wait time in days extracted from the recorded wait-time value divided by 365.0; the reference value is the mean of this score over the organ-specific reference population, and both displayed scores are rounded to four decimals.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Rows are grouped by organ and ordered within each organ by higher Patient Urgency Score first; no limit is requested.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata confirmed ECMO and VAD values in recipients_immunology.life_support and showed that clinical.med_urgency includes bare '2' and '3' variants while clinical.wait_time stores day counts as text, so the derivation now normalizes these representations.

question:
I'm wondering if how we ship organs really makes a difference. Can you run some numbers for me?
Let's look at all our finished transplants.
Group them by how the organ was transported—you know, ground, helicopter, commercial air, all that.
For each of those transport types, I want to see the average Total Ischemia Time rounded to two decimals, and the average Expected Graft Survival Score rounded to four decimals.
Sort the results so I can see which transport methods are linked with the best outcomes.
evidence:
[2] Total Ischemia Time
Description: Measures the total time an organ is without blood supply, from recovery to transplant.
Definition: The sum of the time from organ recovery to preservation and the time from preservation to transplant. Formula: $T_{ischemia} = T_{cold} + T_{warm}$

[4] HLA Mismatch Score
Description: Quantifies the degree of immunological difference between a donor and recipient based on Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA).
Definition: A count of the mismatched HLA antigens (A, B, DR) between the donor and recipient. Formula: $S_{mismatch} = \sum_{i \in \{A, B, DR\}} (HLA_i^{donor} \neq HLA_i^{recipient})$

[20] ABO Blood Type Compatibility
Description: Defines the rules for matching blood types between an organ donor and recipient to prevent hyperacute rejection.
Definition: A fundamental matching rule where recipient blood type determines acceptable donor types. Type O is the universal donor; Type AB is the universal recipient. Type A can receive from A and O. Type B can receive from B and O.

[10] Immunological Compatibility Score
Description: A comprehensive score assessing the immunological match, factoring in blood type and HLA differences.
Definition: A weighted score based on ABO blood type compatibility status and the HLA Mismatch Score. Formula: $S_{immune} = 0.6 \times I_{ABO} + 0.4 \times (1 - \frac{S_{mismatch}}{6})$, where $I_{ABO}$ is 1 for compatible, 0 otherwise.

[13] Expected Graft Survival (EGS) Score
Description: Predicts the probability of a transplanted organ functioning successfully over a specific period.
Definition: A predictive score based on factors like the Immunological Compatibility Score and donor age. Formula: $EGS = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(-0.5 + 1.5 S_{immune} - 0.02 Age_{donor})}}$

[21] Cold Ischemia
Description: The period during which a harvested organ is kept cold to preserve it, starting from when its blood supply is cut off until it is transplanted.
Definition: A state of organ preservation where metabolic activity is slowed by cooling, typically to around 4°C, to minimize tissue damage while outside the body. This is a critical factor in transplant success.

[8] Logistical Feasibility Index
Description: Calculates an index representing the logistical viability of a transplant, considering distance and expected organ preservation time.

Description: A score assessing the risk associated with the transplant surgery itself.
Definition: A composite score derived from the recipient's comorbidities and the inherent complexity of the surgical procedure. Formula: $S_{surgical} = 0.6 \times N_{comorbidities} + 0.4 \times C_{procedure}$, where components are normalized.

Description: The presence of one or more additional diseases or conditions co-occurring with a primary disease or condition.
Definition: In transplantation, a recipient's pre-existing conditions (e.g., diabetes, heart disease) are considered comorbidities. They can increase the complexity and risk of the transplant procedure.

question:
I want to know if our fancy Decision Support System is actually helping us pick better matches. Can you check if its score lines up with the EGS score?
Please take all our completed transplants and divide them into 5 groups based on their DSS score. For each of these 5 buckets, tell me how many transplants are in it and what their average Expected Graft Survival Score is, rounded to four decimals. I want to see if the average EGS score goes up as the DSS score bucket goes up.
evidence:
[4] HLA Mismatch Score
Description: Quantifies the degree of immunological difference between a donor and recipient based on Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA).
Definition: A count of the mismatched HLA antigens (A, B, DR) between the donor and recipient. Formula: $S_{mismatch} = \sum_{i \in \{A, B, DR\}} (HLA_i^{donor} \neq HLA_i^{recipient})$

[20] ABO Blood Type Compatibility
Description: Defines the rules for matching blood types between an organ donor and recipient to prevent hyperacute rejection.
Definition: A fundamental matching rule where recipient blood type determines acceptable donor types. Type O is the universal donor; Type AB is the universal recipient. Type A can receive from A and O. Type B can receive from B and O.

[10] Immunological Compatibility Score
Description: A comprehensive score assessing the immunological match, factoring in blood type and HLA differences.
Definition: A weighted score based on ABO blood type compatibility status and the HLA Mismatch Score. Formula: $S_{immune} = 0.6 \times I_{ABO} + 0.4 \times (1 - \frac{S_{mismatch}}{6})$, where $I_{ABO}$ is 1 for compatible, 0 otherwise.

[13] Expected Graft Survival (EGS) Score
Description: Predicts the probability of a transplanted organ functioning successfully over a specific period.
Definition: A predictive score based on factors like the Immunological Compatibility Score and donor age. Formula: $EGS = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(-0.5 + 1.5 S_{immune} - 0.02 Age_{donor})}}$

[28] Graft Survival
Description: Refers to the period of time a transplanted organ continues to function properly within the recipient's body.
Definition: A key outcome measure in transplantation. Successful Graft Survival means the organ is performing its intended biological functions without signs of rejection or failure.

rc_round1.row_grain: One of the five DSS-score buckets for completed transplants.

rc_round2.derivation: Partition the completed transplants into five ordered buckets based on DSS score, with the bucket boundaries or partitioning method unspecified, and compute the transplant count and average stored Expected Graft Survival Score for each bucket, rounding the average to four decimal places.

Definition: The number of mismatches impacts rejection risk. A '0-mismatch' is a perfect HLA match and is ideal. A '6-mismatch' is a complete mismatch across the A, B, and DR loci, representing the highest immunological barrier outside of ABO or positive crossmatch issues.

question:
I need to see the trade-offs we're making with our less-than-perfect donor organs.
Can you pull a list of all matches that fall under our Marginal Donor Acceptance Criteria? That means either the age gap is huge—more than 25 years—or their kidney score is poor, say under 40.
For each of those matches, show me the donor and patient IDs, tell me exactly why we're calling the donor 'marginal', and then calculate the patient's standard Patient Urgency Score so I can see just how desperate they are. Round the score to four decimals. Sort it so the most urgent patients are at the top.
evidence:
[3] Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR)
Description: Estimates the kidney's filtration capacity, a key indicator of renal function.
Definition: A calculated rate based on serum creatinine level, age, and gender. A simplified estimation formula is: $eGFR = 141 \times (\frac{Cr}{0.9})^{-0.411} \times 0.993^{Age}$ (for males, where Cr is serum creatinine). The actual formula can be more complex.

[9] Renal Function Score
Description: A composite score to evaluate a donor's kidney health based on key indicators.
Definition: A score calculated from the donor's Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) and serum creatinine (Cr) level. Formula: $S_{renal} = (1.0 \times eGFR) - (10.0 \times Cr)$.

[5] Recipient Wait Time Ratio
Description: Calculates the ratio of a recipient's waiting time to the average waiting time for their specific organ and blood type.
Definition: The recipient's wait time in days converted to years. Formula: $R_{wait} = \frac{T_{recipient_wait_days}}{365.0}$

[25] Medical Urgency Status
Description: A classification system used to prioritize patients on the transplant waiting list based on their immediate need and risk of mortality.
Definition: A tiered system that reflects how critically ill a patient is. For calculation purposes, statuses are mapped to numerical values: Status 1A is assigned a value of 5, Status 1B is 4, Status 2 is 3, and Status 3 is 2. All other statuses are assigned a value of 1.

[14] Patient Urgency Score
Description: A score that quantifies the urgency of a recipient's need for a transplant.
Definition: A composite score based on the recipient's medical urgency status and their Recipient Wait Time Ratio. Formula: $S_{urgency} = 0.7 \times Status_{medical} + 0.3 \times R_{wait}$

rc_round1.population: All donor-patient matches where the absolute donor-patient age gap is greater than 25 years or the donor's kidney score is below 40, where kidney score is the donor Renal Function Score (1.0 × eGFR − 10.0 × serum creatinine).
rc_round1.row_grain: Each row represents one donor-patient match that satisfies the marginal-donor criteria.
rc_round1.column_role: Each row must show the donor ID, patient ID, the applicable marginal-donor reason or reasons, and the patient's Patient Urgency Score rounded to four decimal places.
rc_round1.derivation: For each eligible match, compute the Patient Urgency Score as 0.7 times the mapped Medical Urgency Status (1A=5, 1B=4, 2=3, 3=2, other=1) plus 0.3 times the Recipient Wait Time Ratio (recipient wait time in days divided by 365.0), round it to four decimal places, and represent the marginal reason as the satisfied age-gap criterion, kidney-score criterion, or both.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Order rows by Patient Urgency Score in descending order; tie-breaking is unspecified.

rc_round2.population: All donor-patient matches where the absolute donor-patient age gap is greater than 25 years or the donor's kidney score is below 40, where kidney score is the donor Renal Function Score (1.0 × eGFR − 10.0 × serum creatinine).
rc_round2.row_grain: Each row represents one donor-patient match that satisfies the marginal-donor criteria.
rc_round2.column_role: Each row must show the donor ID, patient ID, the applicable marginal-donor reason or reasons, and the patient's Patient Urgency Score rounded to four decimal places.
rc_round2.derivation: For each eligible match, compute the Patient Urgency Score as 0.7 times the mapped Medical Urgency Status plus 0.3 times the Recipient Wait Time Ratio, then round to four decimal places. Map Status 1A to 5, Status 1B to 4, Status 2 to 3, Status 3 to 2, and other statuses to 1, treating bare '2' and '3' as Status 2 and Status 3. Use numeric donor age, donor eGFR, donor serum creatinine, and recipient wait days extracted from their recorded representations; divide recipient wait days by 365.0. Compute the donor Renal Function Score as 1.0 × donor eGFR − 10.0 × donor serum creatinine, and represent the marginal reason as the satisfied age-gap criterion, kidney-score criterion, or both.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Order rows by Patient Urgency Score in descending order; tie-breaking is unspecified.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata resolved that clinical.med_urgency may contain bare '2' or '3', and that donor age, donor creatinine, and recipient wait days are stored in textual forms requiring numeric parsing. It also identifies function_and_recovery.don_gfr_val and don_crtn_val as the donor eGFR and creatinine inputs for the renal-function score.

Definition: A fundamental matching rule where recipient blood type determines acceptable donor types. Type O is the universal donor; Type AB is the universal recipient. Type A can receive from A and O. Type B can receive from B and O.

[10] Immunological Compatibility Score
Description: A comprehensive score assessing the immunological match, factoring in blood type and HLA differences.
Definition: A weighted score based on ABO blood type compatibility status and the HLA Mismatch Score. Formula: $S_{immune} = 0.6 \times I_{ABO} + 0.4 \times (1 - \frac{S_{mismatch}}{6})$, where $I_{ABO}$ is 1 for compatible, 0 otherwise.

[13] Expected Graft Survival (EGS) Score
Description: Predicts the probability of a transplanted organ functioning successfully over a specific period.
Definition: A predictive score based on factors like the Immunological Compatibility Score and donor age. Formula: $EGS = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(-0.5 + 1.5 S_{immune} - 0.02 Age_{donor})}}$

[4] HLA Mismatch Score
Description: Quantifies the degree of immunological difference between a donor and recipient based on Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA).
Definition: A count of the mismatched HLA antigens (A, B, DR) between the donor and recipient. Formula: $S_{mismatch} = \sum_{i \in \{A, B, DR\}} (HLA_i^{donor} \neq HLA_i^{recipient})$

[44] HLA Mismatch Levels
Description: Illustrates the significance of the number of HLA mismatches.
Definition: The number of mismatches impacts rejection risk. A '0-mismatch' is a perfect HLA match and is ideal. A '6-mismatch' is a complete mismatch across the A, B, and DR loci, representing the highest immunological barrier outside of ABO or positive crossmatch issues.

[22] Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) Typing
Description: The process of identifying specific HLA protein markers on a person's cells to match a donor with a recipient for transplantation.
Definition: A genetic test that identifies a person's unique HLA markers. A closer HLA match between a donor and recipient reduces the risk of the recipient's immune system attacking, or rejecting, the transplanted organ.

evidence:
[25] Medical Urgency Status
Description: A classification system used to prioritize patients on the transplant waiting list based on their immediate need and risk of mortality.
Definition: A tiered system that reflects how critically ill a patient is. For calculation purposes, statuses are mapped to numerical values: Status 1A is assigned a value of 5, Status 1B is 4, Status 2 is 3, and Status 3 is 2. All other statuses are assigned a value of 1.

[4] HLA Mismatch Score
Description: Quantifies the degree of immunological difference between a donor and recipient based on Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA).

[34] Allocation Policy
Description: The specific versioned set of rules governing organ distribution, used to prioritize recipients.
Definition: The precise set of rules used for organ distribution, identified by a unique version string in the `allc_pol_vers` field, such as 'v2.7'[cite: 73]. Each policy embodies a strict hierarchy of rules. As a formal example, a given policy stipulates that Medical Urgency Status is the primary sorting criterion; for recipients with an identical urgency status, the one with a lower HLA Mismatch Score receives higher priority.

[21] Cold Ischemia
Description: The period during which a harvested organ is kept cold to preserve it, starting from when its blood supply is cut off until it is transplanted.
Definition: A state of organ preservation where metabolic activity is slowed by cooling, typically to around 4°C, to minimize tissue damage while outside the body. This is a critical factor in transplant success.

[36] Regional Allocation Priority
Description: A core principle within transplant allocation that prioritizes local matches to enhance fairness and clinical outcomes.
Definition: A core rule embedded within an Allocation Policy that gives priority to recipients located in the same geographic region as the donor. [cite_start]This principle is implemented by matching the donor's region with the recipient's `allc_region`[cite: 72]. The primary goals are to ensure equitable organ access for the local community and to improve medical outcomes by minimizing the Cold Ischemia time associated with long-distance transport.

[20] ABO Blood Type Compatibility
Description: Defines the rules for matching blood types between an organ donor and recipient to prevent hyperacute rejection.
Definition: A fundamental matching rule where recipient blood type determines acceptable donor types. Type O is the universal donor; Type AB is the universal recipient. Type A can receive from A and O. Type B can receive from B and O.

question:
I need to know if we're getting less bang for our buck on the really urgent transplants.
Can you run a cost-effectiveness analysis for me? For every completed transplant, figure out the CER. Let's just assume the quality-adjusted life year gain is 8 years times whatever their quality-of-life score is.
Then, I want you to group the results by the patient's medical urgency status. Show me the average CER, rounded to two decimal places, for the Status 1A patients, the Status 1B patients, and so on. Keep them in order of urgency.
evidence:
[11] Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
Description: A measure of disease burden, including both the quality and the quantity of life lived.
Definition: Calculated by multiplying the years of life by a quality-of-life score. Formula: $QALY = Years_{life} \times Quality_{score}$

[12] Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (CER)
Description: Calculates the cost per unit of health outcome, often using Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY).
Definition: The ratio of the net cost of an intervention to its net health gain. Formula: $CER = \frac{Cost_{net}}{QALY_{gained}}$

[25] Medical Urgency Status
Description: A classification system used to prioritize patients on the transplant waiting list based on their immediate need and risk of mortality.
Definition: A tiered system that reflects how critically ill a patient is. For calculation purposes, statuses are mapped to numerical values: Status 1A is assigned a value of 5, Status 1B is 4, Status 2 is 3, and Status 3 is 2. All other statuses are assigned a value of 1.

[48] Cost-Effectiveness Thresholds
Description: Illustrates typical thresholds for considering a medical intervention as cost-effective.
Definition: A common benchmark for the Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (CER) in the US is $50,000 to $150,000 per Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) gained. Interventions below this threshold are generally considered a good value.

rc_round1.population: All completed transplant events, each considered within the patient's medical urgency status.
rc_round1.row_grain: One row for each patient medical urgency status group among the completed transplants.
rc_round1.column_role: The medical urgency status and the corresponding average CER.
rc_round1.derivation: For each completed transplant, compute QALY gain as 8 years multiplied by the patient's quality-of-life score, compute CER as net cost divided by that QALY gain, then average the transplant-level CER values within each medical urgency status and round the average to two decimal places.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Order the status groups by descending mapped urgency value, with Status 1A = 5, Status 1B = 4, Status 2 = 3, Status 3 = 2, and all other statuses = 1; ordering among tied statuses is unspecified.

rc_round2.population: All completed transplant events, each considered within the patient's medical urgency status.
rc_round2.row_grain: One row for each canonical patient medical urgency status group among the completed transplants.
rc_round2.column_role: The canonical medical urgency status and the corresponding average CER.
rc_round2.derivation: For each completed transplant event, compute QALY gain as 8 years multiplied by the recipient's quality-of-life assessment score recorded for that transplant, and compute CER as the transplant's estimated procedure and logistics cost, treated as net cost, divided by that QALY gain. Group by canonical medical urgency status, treating recorded bare '2' and '3' as Status 2 and Status 3, then average the transplant-level CER values within each status and round the average to two decimal places.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Order the canonical status groups by descending mapped urgency value, with Status 1A = 5, Status 1B = 4, Status 2 = 3, Status 3 = 2, and all other statuses = 1; recorded bare '2' and '3' are interpreted as Status 2 and Status 3 for this ordering. Ordering among tied statuses is unspecified.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata showed clinical.med_urgency may contain bare '2' and '3' variants, so the contract normalizes them to Status 2 and Status 3 before grouping and ordering. [17] Predictive Maintenance Urgency (PMU)
Description: A score that quantifies the urgency of performing maintenance based on predictive models.
Definition: A risk score combining remaining useful life (RUL) and fault prediction. Formula: (1000 / (rulhours + 1)) + (faultpredscore * 10).

[4] Average Joint Temperature
Description: Calculates the average temperature across all of the robot's joints.
Definition: The mean temperature across all six joints (J1 to J6). Formula: (J1_temp + ... + J6_temp) / 6.

[9] Joint Temperature Differential
Description: Measures the temperature difference between the hottest and coolest joints, which can indicate localized issues.
Definition: The difference between the maximum and minimum temperature across all six joints (J1 to J6). Formula: GREATEST(J1_temp, ..., J6_temp) - LEAST(J1_temp, ..., J6_temp).

[43] Thermal Anomaly
Description: Identifies a potential thermal issue in a robot's joints based on temperature deviations.
Definition: A Thermal Anomaly is flagged if the Average Joint Temperature exceeds 75°C or if the Joint Temperature Differential is greater than 15°C.

[48] Predictive Maintenance Trigger
Description: A rule that triggers a high-priority maintenance work order based on predictive data.
Definition: A Predictive Maintenance Trigger is activated if the Predictive Maintenance Urgency (PMU) score is greater than 50.

rc_round1.population: Robots whose Predictive Maintenance Urgency score is greater than 50 and whose thermal state is anomalous because the average joint temperature exceeds 75°C or the joint temperature differential exceeds 15°C.
rc_round1.row_grain: One qualifying robot.
rc_round1.column_role: Robot ID, robot model, Predictive Maintenance Urgency score, and hottest joint temperature.
rc_round1.derivation: For each qualifying robot, compute the Predictive Maintenance Urgency score as (1000 / (rulhours + 1)) + (faultpredscore * 10) and compute the hottest joint temperature as the maximum temperature among joints J1 through J6.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Order qualifying robots with worst cases first, but the ranking criterion for worstness is not specified.

rc_round2.population: Robots whose Predictive Maintenance Urgency score is greater than 50 and whose thermal state is anomalous because the average joint temperature exceeds 75°C or the joint temperature differential exceeds 15°C.
rc_round2.row_grain: One qualifying robot.
rc_round2.column_role: Robot ID, robot model, Predictive Maintenance Urgency score, and hottest joint temperature.
rc_round2.derivation: For each qualifying robot, compute the Predictive Maintenance Urgency score as (1000 / (rulhours + 1)) + (faultpredscore * 10), and compute the hottest joint temperature as the maximum temperature among the robot's six joint temperatures (J1 through J6), using joint temperature readings rather than gearbox temperatures.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Order qualifying robots with worst cases first, but the ranking criterion for worstness is not specified.
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata confirms that per-joint temperatures are stored in joint_condition.joint_condition as temperature_C, while mechanical_status.component_status gearboxes store gearbox temperatures; this validates using joint temperatures, not gearbox temperatures, for the hottest joint temperature. No other Round-1 semantic commitments were changed.

question: Find robots doing precision work that aren't accurate enough, showing their ID, job, error amount, and if they need calibration.
evidence:
[8] Relative Positional Error
Description: Normalizes the Cartesian position error against the robot's maximum reach to provide a scale-independent accuracy metric.
Definition: The robot's positional error as a fraction of its maximum reach. Formula: positional_error_mm / reach_mm.

[41] Precision-Critical Applications
Description: An enumeration of robot applications that demand the highest degree of positional and orientational accuracy.
Definition: Precision-Critical Applications include 'Assembly', 'Electronics-Handling', 'Inspection', 'Dispensing', and 'Laser Cutting'.

[50] Precision Performance Degradation
Description: Evaluates if a robot's accuracy is suitable for its task.
Definition: Precision Performance Degradation is flagged if the Relative Positional Error exceeds 0.0001.

rc_round1.population: Robots whose job is one of the precision-critical applications ('Assembly', 'Electronics-Handling', 'Inspection', 'Dispensing', 'Laser Cutting') and whose relative positional error exceeds 0.0001.
rc_round1.row_grain: One robot.
rc_round1.column_role: Robot ID, job/application, relative positional error amount, and an indicator of whether calibration is needed.
rc_round1.derivation: The error amount is the relative positional error metric, defined as positional error divided by maximum reach, and calibration need is flagged when that metric exceeds 0.0001.
rc_round1.filter_policy: none

rc_round2.population: Robots, identified by robot code, whose job/application is one of the precision-critical applications ('Assembly', 'Electronics-Handling', 'Inspection', 'Dispensing', 'Laser Cutting') and whose relative positional error exceeds 0.0001.
rc_round2.row_grain: One robot (one robot code).
rc_round2.column_role: Robot ID (unique robot code), job/application, relative positional error amount, and an indicator of whether calibration is needed.
rc_round2.derivation: The error amount is the relative positional error metric, defined as positional error divided by maximum reach, and calibration need is flagged when that metric exceeds 0.0001.
rc_round2.filter_policy: none
rc_round2.meta_review: Metadata resolves robot identity to the unique robot code (robot_record.botcode), distinguishing it from record registration identifiers. No other metadata refinement was accepted.

question: Show me robots working too hard right now, listing their model, how much payload capacity they're using, and their cycle speed. Make sure the most overloaded ones are at the top of the list.
evidence:
[1] Payload Utilization Ratio (PUR)
Description: Measures the ratio of the robot's actual working payload to its maximum rated payload capacity, indicating how heavily it is loaded.
Definition: The proportion of the robot's maximum lifting capacity being used. Formula: actual_payload_weight / payload_capacity_kg.

[12] Throughput Rate
Description: Calculates the number of cycles completed per minute, as a direct measure of production throughput.
Definition: The number of program cycles a robot completes per minute. Formula: 60 / cycle_time_seconds.

[58] Intensive Workload
Description: Identifies a robot that is consistently operating at a high intensity level.
Definition: A robot has an 'Intensive Workload' if its Payload Utilization Ratio is > 0.8 AND its Throughput Rate is in the top 20th percentile (quintile 1) for its application.

rc_round1.population: Target robots currently meeting the Intensive Workload definition: payload utilization ratio greater than 0.8 and throughput rate in the highest 20% of throughput rates among robots in the same application, with that application-specific throughput distribution serving as the reference population.
rc_round1.row_grain: One qualifying robot.
rc_round1.column_role: The robot's model, payload-capacity utilization, and cycle speed.
rc_round1.derivation: Payload-capacity utilization is the ratio of actual payload weight to rated payload capacity, cycle speed is cycles per minute computed as 60 divided by cycle time in seconds, and the top-20% condition compares the robot's throughput rate with throughput rates in its application.
rc_round1.filter_policy: Order qualifying robots from most to least overloaded using descending payload utilization ratio; tie-breaking is unspecified.

rc_round2.population: Target robots currently meeting the Intensive Workload definition: payload utilization ratio greater than 0.8 and throughput rate in the highest 20% of throughput rates among robots in the same application, with that application-specific throughput distribution serving as the reference population.
rc_round2.row_grain: One qualifying robot.
rc_round2.column_role: The robot's model, payload-capacity utilization, and cycle speed.
rc_round2.derivation: Payload-capacity utilization is the ratio of actual payload weight to rated payload capacity, cycle speed is cycles per minute computed as 60 divided by cycle time in seconds, and the top-20% condition compares the robot's throughput rate with throughput rates in its application.
rc_round2.filter_policy: Order qualifying robots from most to least overloaded using descending payload utilization ratio; tie-breaking is unspecified.
rc_round2.meta_review: No relevant metadata refinement; Round-1 contract preserved.

question: Let's see which manufacturers are struggling the most with their robots' health. For manufacturers with at least two robots getting worse, show me how many are affected and what their average decline rate is. Please show the manufacturer names in lowercase.
evidence:
[0] Robot Age
Description: Calculates the operational age of a robot in days since its commissioning date.
Definition: The duration in days from the robot's installation date to the present. Formula: CURRENT_DATE - installation_date.

[19] Health Degradation Rate (HDR)
Description: Calculates the rate at which the robot's composite health index is declining relative to its age.
Definition: The rate of decline in a robot's health index per day. Formula: (1.0 - condition_index) / robot_age_in_days.

[59] Degrading Robot
Description: Flags a robot whose health is currently deteriorating.
Definition: A robot is considered to be 'Degrading' if its Health Degradation Rate (HDR) is greater than 0.

rc_round1.population: Target manufacturers are those with at least two associated robots whose Health Degradation Rate is greater than 0; the affected robots for each manufacturer are its robots with Health Degradation Rate greater than 0, where HDR is (1.0 - condition_index) divided by robot age in days (CURRENT_DATE - installation_date).
rc_round1.row_grain: One qualifying manufacturer.
rc_round1.column_role: Lowercase manufacturer name, count of affected robots, and average decline rate for those affected robots.
rc_round1.derivation: For each qualifying manufacturer, aggregate its affected robots to count them and compute the mean Health Degradation Rate, rendering the manufacturer name in lowercase.
rc_round1.filter_policy: none

rc_round2.population: Target manufacturers are those with at least two associated robots whose Health Degradation Rate is greater than 0; the affected robots for each manufacturer are its robots with Health Degradation Rate greater than 0, where HDR is (1.0 - condition_index) divided by robot age in days (CURRENT_DATE - installation_date).
rc_round2.row_grain: One qualifying manufacturer.
rc_round2.column_role: Lowercase manufacturer name, count of affected robots, and average decline rate for those affected robots.
rc_round2.derivation: For each qualifying manufacturer, aggregate its affected robots to count them and compute the mean Health Degradation Rate, rendering the manufacturer name in lowercase.
rc_round2.filter_policy: none
rc_round2.meta_review: No relevant metadata refinement; Round-1 contract preserved.
